messages:
Samira: Quick sync — thinking about epochal bucket reconciliation across edge proxies and the central quota service. We keep seeing ~1s+ p99 spikes when the reconcilers run in parallel. want to capture tradeoffs before I write an RFC.
Ben: Are these spikes CPU-bound on the proxy or network/DB contention?
Li: From traces the proxies do a small burst of RPCs to quota-store and we also see a tail from kv-writes in the reconciler. DB IO + lock contention.
Matt: Could be amplification from naive window merging. If each proxy pushes full bucket deltas, central merges are O(n*k).
Samira: Agree — idea: move to epochal summaries + probabilistic sampling so proxies send compact deltas and central does occasional full reconcile. tradeoff: slightly less precise fairness for much lower peak load.
Ben: Sounds promising. How would we keep abuse signals accurate? currently abuse_score influences admission immediately. If we delay reconciliaton we risk stale penalties.
Li: We can keep local short-lived probes for high-risk clients: immediate local penalties + async global amortized updates. That way safety actions remain fast while global fairness converges.
Matt: Prototype config sketch:
```yaml
reconciler:
  send_mode: "epoch_summary" # full|summary|sample
  summary_interval: 20s
  full_reconcile_interval: 15m
  sample_rate: 0.05 # when in sample mode
  max_parallel_syncs: 2
```
Ben: Good. Also consider backpressure: if central is overloaded, proxies should fall back to degraded mode (local-only admission) and flip a metric/flag. ops-bot can alert.
ops-bot: ALERT: central-quota-store cpu > 85% for 5m — initiating soft-degrade policy for proxies with >10k in-flight.
Samira: That alert pattern matches what we want. Need clear interface boundary: proxies must be able to: 1) perform local provisional admits, 2) emit compact epoch summaries, 3) request forced full sync for suspicious clients.
Li: For the "forced full sync" path, we should expose a lightweight RPC: POST /quota/sync?client_id=... which accepts an optional priority header. Keep auth scoped.
Matt: One more thing: telemetry. We need per-proxy metrics: outgoing_sync_size, delta_compression_ratio, sync_latency, reconciliation_stalls. Those will help tune summary_interval vs full_reconcile_interval.
Ben: Operational runbook items: - If central CPU p99 sync latency > 500ms, reduce summary_interval by x? actually increase interval to reduce frequency. - If abuse false positives increase, raise sample_rate temporarily to increase fidelity.
Samira: I'll draft an RFC with three phases: (1) epoch_summary wire format + metrics, (2) adaptive sampling + soft-degrade logic, (3) full rollout + audit hooks.
Li: One blocker: existing client SDKs expect strict global monotonic credits on every request. we'll need a compatibility shim: SDK observes provisional admit and can opt in to strong-consistency checks with a throwaway RPC.
Matt: Could we use a per-client fast-path: small strong-consistency token (nonce) that proxies can fetch cheaply for critical calls? avoids full sync.
Samira: Good idea — add to RFC. For now action items: @Ben to prototype summary serialization compressing repeated client ids; @Li to draft the forced-sync RPC; @Matt to propose metrics+dashboards; I'll assemble RFC + runbook.
Ben: prototyping this week.
Li: will have RPC sketch by Fri.
Matt: dashboard draft Monday.
Samira: Thanks — keeping the change incremental should let us measure unit-cost improvements before any behavioral changes. I'll post the RFC link when ready. :thumbsup:
